title: What’s wrong with Oregon? Upset loss at Oklahoma State casts doubt on No. 6 Ducks’ superteam build
content:
No. 6 Oregon, one of the trendy preseason picks to contend for the national championship, suffered a 39-31 loss at unranked Oklahoma State on Saturday at Boone Pickens Stadium, calling into question whether the Ducks can truly be considered contenders.

The loss was particularly surprising given that Oklahoma State lost at Tulsa just a week ago, rolling out an anemic offense in Eric Morris’ first game as Cowboys head coach. That wasn’t the case on Saturday.

Oklahoma State quarterback Drew Mestemaker outdueled Oregon’s Dante Moore, considered one of the top 2027 NFL Draft prospects. Mestemaker threw for 317 yards and two touchdowns and ran for 109 yards and another score. Moore started 5 of 15 for just 45 yards in the first half before finishing 14 of 29 for 191 yards and two touchdowns.

It is Oklahoma State’s first win since Aug. 28, 2025, when the Cowboys beat UT Martin in their season opener. The win over Oregon broke a 12-game losing streak and marks the first time a team has broken a losing streak of 10 or more games against an opponent ranked in the Associated Press top 10.

“Everybody counted them out, told them how bad they were,” Morris said, with his voice quivering. “Proud of those kids.”

As fans rushed the field, ESPN reporter Taylor McGregor asked Morris what stood out about the moment, which marked his first win at Oklahoma State.

“I don’t know if I can top this,” Morris said. “I’m not gonna retire, but I might think about it tonight.”

Oregon’s offense, under the direction of new coordinator Drew Mehringer after Will Stein was hired to be Kentucky’s head coach, sputtered early on. The Ducks had five empty possessions to start the game, including a trio of three-and-outs.

Eventually, Moore and the passing game got going, as he was able to find receivers Dakorien Moore and Evan Stewart for touchdowns, but things were still uneven. The Ducks struggled to run the ball efficiently, and pass protection was an issue, as Moore was sacked four times.

One late-game offensive sequence was particularly emblematic of Oregon’s day. The Ducks, trailing by five with roughly seven minutes left, had an anemic series, with two Moore pass attempts that were nearly picked off and a toss to Da’Jaun Riggs for 2 yards that set up a fourth-and-8 at their own 33.

Dan Lanning elected to go for it, but the play appeared to be late getting in — the play clock nearly expired before the Ducks got the snap off — and Moore rolled to the right, where there were no open receivers, and threw an incomplete pass that resulted in a turnover on downs.

On the next possession, trailing by eight, the Ducks fumbled and Oklahoma State recovered and was able to run out the clock. Oregon’s last three possessions did not yield any points.

It was Oregon’s first loss to an unranked opponent in the Dan Lanning era. The last time the Ducks lost to an unranked team was Oct. 2, 2021, when Mario Cristobal was still the coach.

The Cowboys looked night-and-day different than a week ago against Tulsa. The Golden Hurricane dominated Oklahoma State’s offensive line, Mestemaker couldn’t get in a rhythm and the Cowboys couldn’t string together many long drives.

On Saturday, they looked different right out of the gate. Mestemaker nearly ran for a touchdown on Oklahoma State’s first play from scrimmage, rushing for 75 yards before stepping out at the 2. There were two key turnovers — Mestemaker had two balls deflected, one of which turned into a pick six and another that was returned to the Oklahoma State 1 — but the Cowboys were undeterred.

They showed offensive balance, with running back Caleb Hawkins (23 rushes, 110 yards) giving Oklahoma State a steady ground presence and keeping some of the pressure off Mestemaker. Receiver Wyatt Young (five catches, 121 yards) made several big plays as well.

Mestemaker, Hawkins and Young are among 19 players who transferred into the program from North Texas, following Morris and several other coaches, where they were 12-2 and made the American Conference Championship Game last year. Oklahoma State added 92 new players this offseason.

Mestemaker’s performance was more in line with preseason expectations. The third-year quarterback led the FBS in passing last season, with 4,379 yards, and was the most important acquisition in Oklahoma State’s top-25 transfer class. He has also been getting first-round draft buzz and redeemed himself with Saturday’s performance, which included an acrobatic 10-yard touchdown run that gave the Cowboys an early fourth-quarter lead.

Oregon has some soul-searching to do. The Ducks survived a close call against Boise State at home last week but were disjointed on Saturday. It’s clearly been a bumpy transition for this team, which is considered one of the most talented in the country but has two new coordinators. The offensive line play, run game and Moore all have to get better if the Ducks have any chance of winning the Big Ten or being a serious factor in the postseason.

It’s a troubling start for what was considered one of the most talented — and expensive — rosters in the country coming into the season.

For Oklahoma State, it’s quite the reversal of fortune. After going winless in the Big 12 each of the last two years, which led to Mike Gundy’s firing, Morris and the Cowboys were taking tons of criticism after getting whipped by Tulsa. This is quite the response and a sign that, perhaps, some of the preseason hype about this team could be justified.
